Know your training

Understand fitness. Train with purpose.

Fitness is not only about lifting weights or burning calories. A balanced programme develops strength, cardiovascular fitness, muscular endurance, mobility and the confidence to move well in everyday life.

1. Strength Training — build a stronger foundation

Strength training uses resistance — such as dumbbells, barbells, machines, cables and bodyweight — to challenge your muscles. With consistent training and gradual progression, your body adapts and becomes stronger.

Why it matters: It helps build and maintain muscle, supports bone health, improves joint stability and posture, makes daily tasks like lifting, climbing stairs and carrying objects easier, and can support healthy body composition when combined with nutrition and activity.

Who can benefit: Beginners, adults, older people, athletes and anyone who wants to improve physical capacity. Exercises and loads should be matched to the person's ability, experience and health status.

2. Conditioning — improve stamina and work capacity

Conditioning trains your body to keep performing during sustained or repeated activity. It can include steady cardio, intervals, circuits, rowing, cycling, running, sled work and other carefully planned exercises.

Why it matters: It develops cardiovascular and respiratory fitness, improves stamina, helps you recover between efforts and makes sports, workouts and everyday activities feel more manageable.

How we approach it: Sessions can combine easy aerobic work, controlled intervals and muscular-endurance circuits. Intensity is progressed gradually, with suitable rest and recovery.

3. HYROX Preparation — strength meets endurance

HYROX is an indoor fitness-racing format that combines running with functional workout stations. Preparation requires more than doing hard circuits: it involves aerobic fitness, pacing, strength endurance, efficient movement and the ability to manage fatigue.

Training focus: Running development, sled-push and sled-pull technique where equipment is available, rowing or ski-erg practice where available, loaded carries, lunges, wall-ball practice and transitions between running and workout stations.

Who it suits: People preparing for a HYROX event as well as members who enjoy structured performance training. Beginners can start with scaled movements and lower training volume before building up.

4. Personal Training — coaching built around you

Personal training is one-to-one coaching shaped around your goals, training history, schedule, movement ability and preferences. A coach can help you understand exercises, select appropriate loads, learn technique and follow a progressive plan.

What is included: Goal discussion, basic fitness and movement review, customised workout planning, exercise demonstrations, technique and form feedback, progress reviews and guidance on training consistency.

Suitable goals: Fat-loss support, muscle building, general fitness, strength development, improved conditioning and HYROX preparation. Results depend on consistency, recovery, nutrition and individual factors.
